'''''Veronica peregrina''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Plantaginaceae|plantain family]] known by several common names including '''neckweed''', '''American speedwell''', '''purslane speedwell''' and '''hairy purslane speedwell'''. It is native to the Americas, and is known on other continents as an [[introduced species]] and a common [[weed]]. It can be weedy in its native range as well, growing on roadsides, on fields, and in other disturbed habitat. It is an annual herb growing from a [[taproot]]. The two subspecies are defined generally on the basis of hairiness: ssp. ''xalapensis'' is coated in glandular hairs and ssp. ''peregrina'' is a hairless variety. The plant produces erect stems up to about {{cvt|30|cm}} tall. The leaves vary in shape from linear to lance-shaped to spoon-shaped with smooth or serrated edges; the lower leaves are borne on [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]]. The [[inflorescence]] is a loose terminal [[raceme]] of flowers and lance-shaped [[bract]]s. The flowers are generally white and {{cvt|2 to 3|mm|frac=32}} wide.

==Taxonomy==
''Veronica peregrina'' was given its scientific name in 1753 by [[Carl Linnaeus]]. It part of the genus [[Veronica (plant)|''Veronica'']], which is classified in the [[Plantaginaceae]] family. It has no [[accepted name|accepted]] subspecies but has two among its {{table row counter|id=Synonyms}} [[Synonym (botany)|synonyms]].<ref name="POWO">{{Cite POWO |last1=POWO |date=2026 |id=812460-1 |title=''Veronica peregrina'' L. |access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref>
